commands.name: summary
commands.summary: memory totals, findings and the largest retainers
commands.details:
Shows process memory by kind, managed and malloc totals, findings, warnings
and the largest retainers. The next list contains commands with addresses
filled in; follow it to inspect the objects behind a finding.

commands.name: verify
commands.summary: object, type and runtime integrity diagnostics
commands.details:
Validates object sizes, MethodTables, GC descriptors, managed references,
runtime thread links, CoreCLR segment and finalization queue boundaries,
and Satori region and finalization-tracker links.
Reports the address, value and reason for each diagnostic. Missing memory
is separate from invalid data. Native pointer fields are not scanned as
managed references. A capture during GC can contain temporary inconsistencies.

Runs without the reference graph, including when ordinary analysis fails.
Reads the dump directly; does not use or rebuild the analysis cache.
Returns 0 when the report is complete, even if it contains diagnostics;
1 on failure. JSON includes exact totals and at most 1,000 details per diagnostic category;
--limit controls how many of those details are printed.

commands.name: types
commands.summary: types by retained, live or dead bytes
options: --match <text>    types whose name contains the text

commands.name: instances
commands.summary: objects of a type, largest first; accepts a full or partial type name
options: --live, --pending, --dead   objects that are live, pending finalization or dead
--text <text>     objects whose string, or identifying string field, contains the text

commands.name: object
commands.summary: object fields, references, root path and native allocations
commands.details:
Accepts any address inside an object. Shows its fields and contents,
objects that reference it, a path from a root, and native memory it owns.
Use retained to see the managed and native bytes that depend on this object.

commands.name: retained
commands.summary: memory retained by an object or chunk; omit the address to list roots
commands.details:
Shows dominator-tree children grouped by type, including managed and
native memory. An address can be inside an object or malloc chunk. Without
an address, lists root sources. Retained bytes are bytes reachable only
through an owner in the detected graph; they are not an RSS prediction.

commands.name: handles
commands.summary: GC handles by handle type and target type

commands.name: regions
commands.summary: heap regions by generation, queue or size; an address selects one region
commands.details:
Without an address, groups regions by generation, queue or size and shows
occupancy. An address selects its containing region, including its memory
totals and object types.

commands.name: threads
commands.summary: thread stacks; a thread ID selects one thread

commands.name: stacks
commands.summary: thread stacks grouped by shared frames
commands.details:
Merges threads by managed frames, from outermost to innermost, and shows
whether each group runs, sleeps, waits for a lock or is otherwise blocked.
Frames are estimated from return addresses; stale frames can split groups.

commands.name: native
commands.summary: glibc allocations by type or referrer, plus arena totals (Linux)
options: --match <text>    groups whose label contains the text
--group <id>      size distribution and allocations for a group
commands.details:
Groups glibc malloc chunks by identified type or reference source, across
all chunk sizes. Each chunk is counted once. Sizes include malloc headers
and padding. --group shows exact-size groups and individual allocations;
use --size to select one size and --limit 0 to list all rows. Use chunk
for reference evidence and malloc-arenas for free memory retained by glibc.
Native pointer matches are conservative; unreferenced chunks are leak candidates.

commands.name: malloc-arenas
commands.summary: free memory retained by glibc arenas and options to release it (Linux)
commands.details:
Separates free chunks from the free end of each heap (the top chunk), and
groups arenas by attached thread count, including arenas whose threads exited.
Shows glibc trim, mmap and arena settings from the dump, plus the estimated
effect of malloc_trim(0), trim_threshold, arena_max and a restart.

commands.name: chunk
commands.summary: a malloc allocation, its owner and its references
commands.details:
Accepts any address inside a malloc chunk. Shows its class or label,
references and path to a root. Managed references use field layouts;
native scans are conservative. Possible managed references are raw address
matches and do not establish retention. Unreferenced chunks are leak candidates.

commands.name: bytes
commands.summary: memory as hex, with pointers resolved to objects or functions
commands.details:
Shows a hex dump and resolves each 8-byte word to an object or function
when possible. --count sets the number of bytes to read.

commands.name: find
commands.summary: locations containing an 8-byte value, such as a pointer or handle
commands.details:
Finds an 8-byte value in object fields, malloc chunks, thread stacks and
other memory. Use it to locate copies of a pointer or GC handle.

commands.name: memory
commands.summary: memory in the dump by kind; with --smaps, resident memory by kind

commands.name: garbage
commands.summary: unreachable objects, grouped by the dead objects that retain them
commands.details:
Shows objects that are unreachable but have not been swept. Each group
starts with a dead object that no other dead object references, and includes
the dead objects reachable only through it. This is not evidence of a leak.

commands.name: fragmentation
commands.summary: dead objects, unused committed space and the survivors that keep it allocated
commands.details:
Shows dead objects and unused committed space, grouped by the GC rule
that keeps it and by the type or owner of the survivors. Each region's space
is attributed to its live objects in proportion to their sizes. GC storage,
objects pending finalization and unparsed bytes are excluded.

commands.name: strings
commands.summary: live strings with the same contents

commands.name: collections
commands.summary: collection capacity and unused slots
commands.details:
Compares backing-array capacity with used slots in live List, Dictionary,
HashSet, Queue and Stack instances. Groups totals by type and gives an
example address to inspect.

commands.name: finalizable
commands.summary: objects with finalizers, grouped by reachability and finalizer state
commands.details:
Separates live registered, live suppressed or immortal, resurrected,
pending-finalization and dead objects. Re-registration can leave an object
pending after its finalizer has run; the dump cannot show its history.

commands.name: zero-arrays
commands.summary: live arrays of 1 KB and more that are at least 90% zero bytes

commands.name: cache
commands.summary: list cached analyses and their disk usage; optionally delete them
options: --delete missing|all|<folder>   remove caches for missing dumps, all dumps or one folder
commands.details:
Lists each cached analysis, its disk usage, last-opened time and source dump.
--delete takes missing, all, or a folder name from this list. It deletes
analysis caches, not source dumps or the live and symbols folders.

commands.name: ps
commands.summary: running .NET processes found through diagnostics sockets
commands.details:
Lists PID, user, program and diagnostics socket for .NET processes found
in TMPDIR and /tmp. Diagnostics must be enabled; capture needs permission
to use the socket.
Process discovery and capture are supported on Linux and macOS.

commands.name: dump
commands.summary: capture a process and print the dump path
options: --out <path>      output file or folder (also -o); defaults to the cache folder
--offline         let the .NET runtime write the dump; pauses for the raw dump write
commands.details:
On Linux, Dotheap copies memory while the process runs, then pauses its
threads to read registers and finish the copy. File and shared mappings
are read again during this pause. Busy processes, large heaps, low memory
and slow storage can cause long pauses. Other processes can still change
shared memory. Requires ptrace access: usually root, or the target user
with suitable process permissions and kernel.yama.ptrace_scope.

Runtime capture requires --offline, including on macOS. It uses the same
.NET diagnostics protocol as dotnet-dump. The process stays paused until
the raw dump is written. Run as the target user or root; the target user
must be able to write to the output directory. Dotheap never switches to
runtime capture automatically when live capture is unavailable or fails.

--out accepts a filename or an existing directory, relative to dotheap's
working directory. A directory gets <program>-<pid>-<time>.dmp.zst.
The default is the cache's live folder. When root requests a runtime dump
of another user's process, the default is a new directory in /tmp.
Existing files are never replaced.

Linux live capture always writes Zstandard data. Runtime capture compresses
after the process resumes, unless the output name omits .zst. If compression
or publication fails, the error gives the raw dump's recovery path.
Linux capture also saves <name>.smaps.zst beside <name>.dmp[.zst] for resident
memory analysis; it is loaded automatically.

Capture fails if the process exits, replaces its address space or cannot
be read at the final pause. Live capture needs space for temporary copies
beside the output. Periodic free-space checks stop capture below 2 GiB.
Runtime capture needs space for both the raw and compressed dump.
The completed path goes to stdout, or {"dump":"<path>"} with --json.
Progress goes to stderr, including the pause count, total pause time
and longest pause.

commands.name: search
commands.summary: search findings, types, methods, native allocations and addresses
commands.details:
Searches findings, report rows (including methods, callbacks and fields),
types and malloc chunk groups. An address reports what occupies that memory.

commands.name: findings
commands.summary: find potential leaks, blocked work and inefficient memory use
commands.details:
Lists findings and the commands for detailed reports.
Each report includes its row count. Use summary for a ranked overview.

commands.name: async
commands.summary: async call chains, awaited operations and shared waits
commands.details:
Shows unfinished async call graphs, including Task.WhenAll, WhenAny and
Task.Run, what the innermost call awaits, and what owns that operation.
Shared waits, synchronous task waits, cycles and isolated waits are listed.
The dump contains no wait durations; matching PDBs can add await source lines.

commands.name: tasks
commands.summary: async calls grouped by stack; an address selects a call or awaited object
commands.details:
Lists running, queued and waiting calls by async stack, with the number
of awaited objects. An address selects a call or the object it awaits.
The result shows calls sharing that wait, their call tree, state-machine
fields and paths from roots. Matching PDBs can add await source lines.

commands.name: arraypool
commands.summary: shared ArrayPool: arrays returned twice, used after return, and dead arrays of pool sizes
commands.details:
Checks shared ArrayPool partitions and thread-local slots. Duplicate slots
indicate a double return; references from live objects can indicate use after
return. Dead arrays of bucket sizes are only missed-return candidates: arrays
allocated directly with those sizes look the same.

commands.name: large-objects
commands.summary: large objects by type and reachability, with unused region space
commands.details:
Uses a size threshold of 85,000 bytes for stock CoreCLR or 32 KB for Satori.
Shows live and dead objects by type. Stock GC results include LOH dead objects
and free gaps; Satori results include committed space beyond huge objects
that occupy their own regions.

commands.name: cancellation
commands.summary: callbacks registered on each CancellationTokenSource
commands.details:
Shows registered callbacks on live CancellationTokenSource objects, grouped
by source and callback method. Undisposed registrations or linked token
sources can keep callback targets and state alive.

commands.name: events
commands.summary: events with many subscribers, grouped by owner
commands.details:
Shows multicast delegates with many subscribers, grouped by the object
and field that hold them and by subscriber type. A long-lived publisher
can keep subscribers alive after they are otherwise unused.

commands.name: timers
commands.summary: timers, their callbacks, awaited operations and owners
commands.details:
Includes Timer, System.Timers.Timer, PeriodicTimer, Task.Delay, Task.WaitAsync
and CancelAfter timers. Shows callback methods or awaiting async calls,
owners and periods. Source lines need matching PDBs. Timer ages are relative
to the latest timer start in the dump, not the capture time.

commands.name: locks
commands.summary: held locks, likely waiting threads and possible deadlocks
commands.details:
Includes lock/Monitor.Enter and System.Threading.Lock. Waiters are inferred
from a lock-enter frame and a stack pointer to a lock held by another thread.
Frames are estimated, so inspect the listed wait chains and possible deadlocks.

commands.name: blocked
commands.summary: threads in synchronous waits, grouped by application frame
commands.details:
Groups synchronous waits such as Task.Wait, GetResult and Monitor.Wait by
the first application frame. Includes busy, blocked and idle thread pool
workers and queued work. Work waiting while workers are blocked can indicate
thread pool starvation; frames are estimated from stack return addresses.

commands.name: network
commands.summary: sockets, HTTP requests, connection pools and pending I/O
commands.details:
Shows socket file descriptors, endpoints, owners and pending reads/writes;
Kestrel and HttpClient requests; HttpClient pools; and socket engines
(epoll on Linux, kqueue on macOS). A pending receive can be an idle connection.
Closed sockets can remain referenced by pooled objects.

commands.name: symbols
commands.summary: download .NET runtime symbols for a Linux dump
commands.details:
Downloads .NET runtime debug files from Microsoft's symbol server, matched
by build ID. Files are cached under dotheap/symbols and reused across dumps
to name native frames. For Satori or another custom runtime, put matching
debug files such as libcoreclr.so.dbg in a --dlls directory.

commands.name: files
commands.summary: managed and native file handles, pending I/O and mapped files
commands.details:
Shows managed file paths, descriptors, access modes, positions, buffered
bytes, pending I/O and owners, plus native paths and mapped files. Native
descriptors are inferred from the integer after a path in a C++ object;
the dump has no kernel file table, so this is not a complete open-file list.

commands.name: connections
commands.summary: pending HTTP requests and socket events
commands.details:
Shows incoming Kestrel requests by stage, outgoing HttpClient requests
awaiting responses or connections, and SocketAsyncEngine events queued for
a worker. Use network for all sockets, requests and connection pools.

commands.name: exceptions
commands.summary: exceptions by type and throwing method, plus unobserved task failures
commands.details:
Groups live and dead exceptions by type and the method in their saved
throw stack. Also groups faulted tasks by exception and observation state.
Many dead exceptions at one site can indicate frequent throwing. Unthrown
exceptions have no saved stack; the dump is not a complete exception history.

commands.name: instance-counts
commands.summary: counts and owners of commonly shared objects, such as HttpClient
commands.details:
Counts live HttpClient instances, handlers, JsonSerializerOptions, Regex,
service providers and other commonly shared or disposable types. Counts at
or above each type's threshold produce findings. Inspect their owners to
distinguish expected usage from unnecessary instances.

commands.name: finalizer-backlog
commands.summary: native memory retained by objects awaiting finalization
commands.details:
Shows malloc memory reachable only through objects pending finalization.
Their finalizers may release it. Inspect the owning types and whether earlier
disposal could have released the native resources.

commands.name: native-held-by-dead
commands.summary: native allocations referenced only by dead managed objects
commands.details:
Shows allocated malloc chunks referenced only by dead managed objects,
grouped by type and field. No pending finalizer remains for those owners.
The memory may have leaked, or malloc may have reused a freed allocation
while the dead object still contains its old address.

commands.name: boxed
commands.summary: boxed primitive and enum values

common: --json            JSON: bytes as numbers, addresses as "0x..." strings; no table truncation
--limit <n>       rows per list (default 20; 0 for all); omitted counts are reported
--dlls <dir>      search recursively for missing assemblies, native binaries and PDBs; repeatable

--smaps <file>    /proc/<pid>/smaps or macOS vmmap output; accepts .zst and .gz
                    default: <name>.smaps.zst, .smaps.gz or .smaps beside <name>.dmp[.zst]
--cache <dir>     save analysis results in this folder instead of the user cache
--no-cache        analyze without a cache; requires an uncompressed dump
--rebuild         process the dump again in the default cache

--native-roots    count pointers in writable native memory as managed roots
                    conservative: stale pointers can keep otherwise dead objects live
--progress        print processing phases to stderr; warnings are always printed

--pid <pid>       capture and analyze instead of <core>; --out and --offline apply
                    see dotheap help dump for permissions, output paths and pauses

sos.dumpheap: `dotheap types <core>` lists types by size (dumpheap -stat), `dotheap instances <core> <type>` the objects of a type (dumpheap -type)
sos.gcroot: `dotheap object <core> <address>` shows the path from an object to a root
sos.dumpobj: `dotheap object <core> <address>` shows the fields of an object
sos.do: `dotheap object <core> <address>` shows the fields of an object
sos.objsize: `dotheap retained <core> <address>` shows what an object keeps alive
sos.eeheap: `dotheap memory <core>` and `dotheap regions <core>` show the memory of the heap
sos.heapstat: `dotheap regions <core>` shows the heap by generation
sos.gcwhere: `dotheap regions <core> <address>` shows the region of an address
sos.clrstack: `dotheap threads <core> <tid>` shows the frames of a thread, `dotheap stacks <core>` all threads merged by their frames
sos.dumpasync: `dotheap tasks <core>` and `dotheap async <core>` show the async calls that wait
sos.finalizequeue: `dotheap finalizable <core>` shows the objects with finalizers
sos.syncblk: `dotheap locks <core>` shows the locks held and the threads that wait for them
sos.verifyheap: `dotheap verify <core>` validates heap and runtime structures
sos.verifyobj: `dotheap verify <core>` reports corrupt objects and their addresses
